hypotheses.mechanism: On axisymmetric bodies, adverse pressure gradient amplifies crossflow vortices (stationary and traveling) that cause early separation; deployed flaps generate streamwise vortices that interact destructively with crossflow modes via vortex-vortex interaction (phase opposition), suppressing crossflow
hypotheses.falsifier: If hot-film measurements show no reduction in crossflow spectral energy (βδ ≈ 0.8) when flaps are deployed, despite confirmed flap deployment and vortex generation, the crossflow suppression mechanism is falsified.

failure_modes.description: Crossflow instability requires a spanwise pressure gradient component, which is absent on axisymmetric bodies at zero yaw. The dominant instability on axisymmetric hulls is Tollmien-Schlichting (TS) waves, not crossflow vortices. Khalil et al. (2015) likely studied yawed bodies or appendages, not the bare axisymmetric stern.
failure_modes.evidence: Boundary layer theory (Schlichting, White): Crossflow instability arises only in 3D boundary layers with crossflow velocity component (e.g., swept wings, cones at incidence). Axisymmetric bodies at zero incidence have 2D boundary layers in meridional planes; N-factor > 9 at Re > 1e8 corresponds to TS transition, not crossflow.

failure_modes.description: Adiabatic compression in water at 18 knots (9.26 m/s) yields ΔT ≈ 0.01°C, not 3°C. Water is nearly incompressible; the temperature rise from stagnation is ΔT = v²/(2·cp) ≈ 43/(2·4184) ≈ 0.005°C. The claimed ΔT ≈ 3°C violates basic thermodynamics of liquid water.
failure_modes.evidence: For water: cp ≈ 4184 J/kg·K, v = 9.26 m/s → dynamic head = v²/2 ≈ 42.9 J/kg → ΔT = 42.9/4184 ≈ 0.01°C. Even with recovery factor r=1, ΔT < 0.02°C. CFD verification claim is physically impossible for liquid water.

failure_modes.description: SMA activation temperature Af = 15°C cannot be reached via adiabatic compression in seawater (typical 4–15°C). With ΔT < 0.02°C, the thermal trigger will never activate. The dual pressure/thermal trigger reduces to pressure-only, but SMA requires temperature change for phase transformation; pressure-gradient alone cannot deploy NiTi flaps without thermal input.
failure_modes.evidence: NiTi SMA actuation requires temperature change through hysteresis loop (Af–As > 0). Pressure-induced martensite transformation in NiTi is negligible at hydrostatic pressures < 100 MPa (submarine depths). Adiabatic heating in water is orders of magnitude too small.

failure_modes.description: Flap height h = 1 mm is far smaller than boundary layer thickness δ at Re = 1e8 (δ ≈ 20–50 mm on submarine stern). Sub-boundary-layer vortex generators (h/δ < 0.05) cannot generate streamwise vortices strong enough to suppress instability modes; they produce negligible circulation (Γ ∝ h²). Wavelength matching λz ≈ 8 mm is arbitrary and unvalidated.
failure_modes.evidence: Submarine stern Re ≈ 1e8 → δ ≈ 0.37·x/Re_x^0.2 ≈ 30 mm at x ≈ 10 m. h/δ ≈ 0.03. Vortex generator effectiveness scales as (h/δ)²; at h/δ < 0.1, vortex circulation is too weak to modify outer-layer instabilities (Lin 2002). Crossflow wavelength on swept wings is O(δ), not 8 mm.

failure_modes.description: The mechanism targets crossflow suppression (Edge B→D), but separation on axisymmetric sterns is driven by adverse-pressure-gradient-induced TS wave growth and separation bubble formation, not crossflow. Streamwise vortices from micro-flaps would primarily enhance momentum transport (Edge C), not suppress non-existent crossflow modes. The claimed mechanism misidentifies the instability physics.
failure_modes.evidence: Axisymmetric separation: Adverse pressure gradient → TS wave amplification → inflectional velocity profile → separation. Crossflow vortices do not exist without spanwise pressure gradient. Saric et al. (2002) results apply only to swept wings (βδ ≈ 0.8 is crossflow parameter for 3D boundary layers).

failure_modes.description: The falsifier (hot-film crossflow spectral energy at βδ ≈ 0.8) will detect no crossflow signal on an axisymmetric model at zero yaw, regardless of flap deployment. A null result would be misinterpreted as mechanism failure rather than hypothesis error. The test cannot distinguish between 'mechanism fails' and 'target instability absent'.
failure_modes.evidence: Hot-film arrays at Re = 5e6 (1:20 model) will measure TS wave spectra (frequency ~ 1–5 kHz), not crossflow. Crossflow requires yaw angle > 5° to appear. The test design assumes crossflow exists; if it doesn't, the falsifier is uninformative.

failure_modes.description: SMA micro-flaps for separation control have been studied (e.g., NASA morphing flaps, Lagoudas 2012), but all target 2D/3D separation via momentum injection (Edge C), not crossflow suppression. The novelty claim of 'unique crossflow suppression on axisymmetric hulls' is invalid because crossflow is not the operative instability.
failure_modes.evidence: Lagoudas (2012) Ch. 12: SMA actuators for marine morphing structures target shock/boundary-layer interaction or 2D separation. No prior art demonstrates crossflow suppression on axisymmetric bodies because the instability does not exist there.
